title: X launches parental controls to help manage teen use
summary: The parental controls feature launch comes some 20 years after X, formerly Twitter, was built

blocks.text: The parental controls feature launch comes some 20 years after X, formerly Twitter, was built

items: Social media platform X has introduced parental controls to help parents guide their teens' usage of the platform.
The controls allow parents to monitor usage time, set limits, approve new followers, and filter content, while ensuring teens maintain ownership of their accounts.
This feature marks the addition of parental controls in X's 20-year history, and is likely a response to concerns about the platform's safety for younger users.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Social media platform X on Thursday, November 26, announced it had introduced parental controls so that parents or guardians could better guide teens on their X usage and experiences on it.
The parental controls will not allow parents or guardians to read private messages, see searches or viewing history, post as their teen, or access a given teen account.

The social media platform, in its announcement, acknowledged that “while X is not designed for or promoted to children, and users must be at least 13 or older where required by law, we take extra care with the young people who are here.”

According to the X announcement, teen accounts “default to protected mode, sensitive media is restricted, and targeted advertising is blocked,” while parental controls give families further tools aside from these standard settings for teens.
The new parental control tools will let parents do the following:

items: see how much time their teen has spent on X over the past week
require approval for new followers (this also makes the account private)
limit For You recommendations and videos to accounts the teen already follows
control who can send direct messages to the account
see which accounts a teen has chatted with one-on-one (without seeing what they’ve written)

blocks.text: The X parental controls announcement is a long time coming. The feature addition is a first after about 20 years of operation, and comes after issues with X’s Grok AI chatbot being a vector for the generation of sexualized images or material featuring women and minors.
According to TechCrunch, while X is not generally aimed at teens, a 2024 study pointed to nearly a third of Gen Alpha kids as having an X account.
Michael O’Herlihy, head of safety at X, said in their press announcement that they aim to strike a balance between parental supervision and letting teens have some freedom to be themselves.

“Parents want practical tools, and teens deserve room to grow,” O’Herlihy said. “With Parental Controls on X, families can set the guardrails that fit their home, while teens keep ownership of their accounts and can see every change.”
A more thorough explanation of the parental control settings is available on this Help Center page. – Rappler.com
